p < j; ++p) {\n                sum = __dadd_rn(sum, __dmul_rn(s[t][p], s[j][p]));\n            }\n            s[t][j] = (s[t][j] - sum) / diag[j];\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    if (t < nb) {\n        for (int j = 0; zeroUpperKernel(double* __restrict__ A, const int n) {\n    const int row = blockIdx.y;\n    const int stride = gridDim.x * blockDim.x;\n    for (int col = row + 1 + blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + zeroUpperKernel(double* __restrict__ A, const int n) {\n    const int row = blockIdx.y;\n    const int stride = gridDim.x * blockDim.x;\n    for (int col = row + 1 + blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + Keeping p sequential\n        // preserves the summation order of the scalar algorithm.\n        double sum = 0.0;\n        if (t >= j && t < nb) {\n            for (int p = 0; p < j; ++p) {\n                sum = __dadd_rn(sum, __dmul_rn(s[t][p], s[j][p]));\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        if (t == j) {\n            const double val = s[j][j] - sum;\n            if (val <= 0.0) {\n                // Matrix is not positive definite; remember the first such column\n                atomicMin(info, k + j);\n            }\n            diag[j] = sqrt(val);\n                                                          const int nb, const int rows) {\n    __shared__ double sL[NB][NB + 1];\n    __shared__ double sX[TRSM_ROWS][NB + 1];\n\n    const int tid = zeroUpperKernel(double* __restrict__ A, const int n) {\n    const int row = blockIdx.y;\n    const int stride = gridDim.x * blockDim.x;\n    for (int col = row + 1 + blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; col < n; col += stride) {\n        A[(size_t)row * n + col] = 0.0;\n    }\n}\n\n__global__ void addDiagonalKernel(double* __restrict__ A, const int n, const double value) {\n    const int double* __restrict__ recon, const double* __restrict__ orig, const size_t count,\n                            double* __restrict__ maxOut, double* __restrict__ relOut) {\n    __shared__ double sMax[256];\n    __shared__ double sRel[256];\n\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n    for (size_t i = (size_t)blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; i < count; i += Blocks entirely above the diagonal are skipped, so only the lower triangle is updated.\n- **One-step look-ahead on two streams**: the panel stream brings the *next* block column up to date and factors it while the update stream is still working on the rest of the trailing submatrix; ordering is enforced with two pairs of alternating events. A narrow (32-wide tile) GEMM instantiation is used for the skinny look-ahead update.\n- **Transfers**: only the lower triangle is uploaded (block-row `cudaMemcpy2D`), which halves H2D volume; the upper triangle is zeroed on the device up front and again at the end (the original's row-wise zeroing, which is unobservable until the end).\n- **Non-positive-definite input** is recorded with `atomicMin` on a device flag and reported after the loop — same message, same column index, same exit status as the original (verified against the reference with a deliberately non-PD matrix).\n- **Matrix generation and validation** also run on the GPU (they were O(n³) and would otherwise dominate). They use the same tiled kernel with *unfused* multiply-add, which reproduces the reference's rounding exactly, so the generated input matrix is bit-identical to the sequential program's.\n\n**Results** (RTX 3090, timings include H2D/D2H, `-v` passes at every size tested: 1, 2, 47, 48, 49, 100, 200, 512, 1000, 2048, 4096, 8192)\n\n| n | sequential | CUDA | speedup |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 512 | 29 ms | 3 ms | ~10× |\n| 1024 | 250 ms | 7 ms | 36× |\n| 2048 | 2135 ms | 21 ms | 102× |\n| 4096 | ~17 s (extrapolated) | 72 ms (318 GFLOPS) | ~240× |\n\nThe dominant trailing-update kernel runs at ~550 GFLOPS FP64, essentially the card's FP64 ceiling; at n=8192 the factorization phase alone sustains 551 GFLOPS. Remaining wall-clock cost is PCIe transfer (~13 GB/s ceiling; pinned memory measured no faster on this box) and, at small n, per-step kernel latency.\n\n`CMakeLists.txt` enables the CUDA language, compiles `cholesky.cpp` with nvcc for sm_80/86 (overridable via `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES`), and keeps the original host flags. No new dependencies; only the CUDA runtime. `compute-sanitizer` memcheck, initcheck, racecheck and synccheck all report zero errors.\n\nTwo notes on fidelity: printed statistics (Sum/Min/Max/Samples) match the sequential run to all 17 digits, but the FNV hash of `L` differs — a blocked parallel factorization cannot reproduce the scalar summation order bit for bit (for n ≤ 48 it does, since that is a single diagonal block).
